title: Knowledge Check 5 - Lessons 21-25
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 21-25 - Access to Records. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: An architect must ensure access to a child object exactly mirrors access to its parent and cannot diverge. Which relationship is appropriate?
questions.explanation: Master-detail couples child access to the parent via Controlled by Parent. Lookup relationships keep access independent, which is the opposite requirement.

questions.question: A user can read a parent Account but cannot read its lookup-child custom object records. Why?
options: The child OWD is Controlled by Parent
Lookup children do not inherit access from the parent; each object shares independently
questions.explanation: Lookup relationships do not propagate access; the child's OWD/sharing governs its own records even when the parent is shared. Only master-detail (or explicit related-record sharing) couples them.

questions.question: Which is a security implication of a master-detail rollup SUM field on the parent?
options: It lets a user who can read the parent see an aggregate total computed from children they cannot individually access
questions.explanation: Rollups compute on the master, so the aggregate is visible with parent access even where individual child access is restricted - a data-exposure trade-off to design around.

questions.question: Sensitive child records must NOT be visible just because a user can read the parent. Which design avoids propagation?
options: A lookup relationship with the child object's OWD kept Private and no related-record sharing
An Account Team on the parent
questions.explanation: Lookups do not propagate access, and keeping the child OWD Private (with no related-record sharing) prevents parent access from leaking to children. Master-detail and related-record sharing would couple them.

questions.question: Which statement about cumulative sharing is TRUE?
options: Each access layer is mutually exclusive
A user's effective access is the UNION of OWD, hierarchy, sharing rules, teams, and relationship propagation - so map them together
questions.explanation: Effective access is the union of all layers; mapping the combination is essential because multiple layers can jointly expose a record even when each is individually correct.

questions.question: What is the role of record types in record access?
options: They shape page layouts, business process, and picklist values without changing the sharing table
They grant access to related records
questions.explanation: Record types are presentation/process controls; they do not alter record-level sharing, which is governed by OWD, hierarchy, rules, teams, and relationship propagation.

questions.question: A complex, data-derived access rule cannot be expressed with sharing rules. What is the appropriate mechanism?
options: A public group with static rules
Apex Managed Sharing inserting Share rows with a custom RowCause
questions.explanation: Apex Managed Sharing grants record access programmatically where declarative rules cannot. Public OWD over-exposes, and groups/record types cannot express dynamic data-derived access.

questions.question: Which requirement is needed to insert Apex Managed Sharing rows for an object?
options: Modify All on the object for the sharing user
questions.explanation: Modify All on the object is required to create/delete managed share rows; lesser permissions cannot insert shares.

questions.question: What does the RowCause field on a Share record represent?
options: The reason why the share row was created (e.g. your custom managed-sharing reason)
questions.explanation: RowCause records the origin/reason of the share (Manual, Rule, or a custom reason) so you can identify and manage managed-sharing rows. Access level is a separate field.

questions.question: An org needs record access based on a value computed from a third-party integration, which the sharing-rule builder cannot express. What is the correct solution?
options: Apex Managed Sharing with a scheduled/triggered reconciliation of Share rows
questions.explanation: Runtime-derived access from external data cannot be a declarative rule; Apex Managed Sharing with reconciliation code is the mechanism. The other options cannot express the dynamic condition.

questions.question: Why must managed sharing code actively remove stale share rows?
options: Managed shares are physical rows that persist; the platform does not auto-recalculate them like rules
questions.explanation: Managed share rows are persistent physical records; because they are not platform-recalculated, your code must insert and delete them as the governing data changes.

questions.question: Which is the best way to keep managed-sharing volume and DML low?
options: Insert shares in a per-record trigger unconditionally
Compute the delta (new needed, existing unnecessary) and insert/delete in batches within one transaction
Use a different RowCause per record
questions.explanation: Reconciling the delta in batches minimizes both DML governors and sharing-table growth. Unconditional per-record inserts bloat sharing and can hit limits.

questions.question: An authenticated partner user must see the Cases belonging to their partner Account. Which is the appropriate sharing configuration?
options: A sharing set mapping the user's Account to Case access
A public group with a criteria rule
Setting Case OWD to Public Read Only
questions.explanation: Sharing sets grant external users access based on their account/contact relationship - the correct portal pattern. Public groups, OWD relaxation, and internal teams do not key off the portal user's account.

questions.question: What is the difference between an authenticated external user and the guest user in Experience Cloud?
options: The guest user is the unauthenticated profile with its own restricted sharing; authenticated external users have a profile/license and relationship-based sharing
questions.explanation: The guest profile represents anonymous visitors with minimal, explicit guest sharing; authenticated external users carry a portal license/profile and access via sharing sets tied to their account.

questions.question: A portal feature expected for partners is unavailable for external users. What is the most likely cause?
options: The portal license tier does not include that feature/object
questions.explanation: Experience Cloud license tiers gate features and object access for external users; an unavailable feature is frequently a license-level limitation rather than a sharing config issue.
